label: Heart
function: Pumps blood around the body. Your pulse and blood pressure show how hard it is working.
spaceRisks: Fluid shifts toward the head in microgravity and changes blood pressure.
Without exercise the heart muscle can weaken.
Long-term radiation exposure may raise cardiovascular risk.

label: Brain
function: Controls thinking, mood, sleep and every other organ.
spaceRisks: Disturbed sleep and day/night rhythm reduce alertness.
Isolation and confinement can cause anxiety and irritability.
High CO2 in closed spaces can cause headache and drowsiness.

label: Lungs
function: Bring oxygen into the blood. Blood oxygen (SpO2) shows how well that works.
spaceRisks: Cabin air quality and CO2 level affect breathing.
Dust particles behave differently in low gravity.
Low SpO2 can be an early sign of a serious problem.

label: Bones
function: Support the body and store calcium.
spaceRisks: Bone density drops without the load of gravity.
Regular resistance exercise is needed to slow the loss.

label: Muscles
function: Move the body and keep posture.
spaceRisks: Muscles weaken quickly when they do not work against gravity.
Daily exercise is part of the mission schedule.

label: Immune system
function: Defends the body against infection. Body temperature is a simple sign of its activity.
spaceRisks: Stress, radiation and disturbed sleep can change immune response.
A fever far from Earth needs attention early.

label: Metabolism
function: Turns food into energy. Blood glucose shows how well the body handles it.
spaceRisks: Changes in diet, activity and sleep can shift blood sugar.
Reduced appetite is common in the first days of spaceflight.
